steps.message:
The unit tests of the `stockroom` package in /app fail intermittently on CI. The output of recent CI runs is in /app/logs/ci, the runner that produced it is /app/tools/ci.py, and /app/docs describes the package; /app/docs/testing.md explains the runner, its logs and how failures are triaged.

Find every root cause of the intermittent failures in the logs and fix it. Write /app/flaky-report.json with one entry per root cause:

    {"causes": [{"class": "<class>", "file": "<path>", "line": <number>, "tests": ["<test id>", ...]}, ...]}

- `class`: one of the classes in /app/docs/testing.md section 4.3.
- `file` and `line`: the module, as a path relative to /app (for example `stockroom/units.py`), and the number of a line that is wrong, counted in the file as you received it, before your changes.
- `tests`: the id of every test that failed in the logs because of this root cause, as the logs print it.

Failures in the logs that do not come from a defect in the current code get no entry and are not listed under any cause.

Then fix the package code under /app/stockroom so that the tests pass in any order, under any `PYTHONHASHSEED`, in any timezone and on any date. Do not change anything under /app/tests, /app/tools, /app/docs or /app/logs. The package will also be run against other tests that follow the docs.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app; cat docs/testing.md; ls -R docs stockroom tests logs tools | head -80; wc -l stockroom/*.py tools/ci.py

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; cat docs/testing.md; ls -R docs stockroom tests logs tools | head -80; wc -l stockroom/*.py tools/ci.py

results.content:
# Testing

## 1. Unit tests

1.1 The tests live in `tests/` and use `unittest` only. From the project root:

    python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

runs them in the order `unittest` picks (modules, classes and methods sorted
by name), in one process, with whatever `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `TZ` and clock the
shell has.

1.2 Every test must pass alone and in any company: in any order, under any
hash seed, in any timezone and on any date. Tests do not use module or class
fixtures (`setUpModule`, `setUpClass`); each test builds what it needs.

1.3 Fixtures are under `tests/fixtures/`. Tests write files only in their
own temporary directories.

## 2. The CI runner

2.1 `tools/ci.py` runs the tests the way CI does. CI starts it on every push,
on one of six runners. Each runner keeps the timezone of the site it runs at:

| Runner | `TZ` |
|---|---|
| `ci-01` | `UTC` |
| `ci-02` | `America/Los_Angeles` |
| `ci-03` | `Europe/Berlin` |
| `ci-04` | `Asia/Tokyo` |
| `ci-05` | `Pacific/Auckland` |
| `ci-06` | `America/Sao_Paulo` |

2.2 The runner collects every test id, sorts them and shuffles them with a
seed, then runs all of them in that order in one child process, one at a
time. A test therefore runs after a random selection of other tests in the
same process.

2.3 The child gets a random `PYTHONHASHSEED`, the runner's `TZ`,
`STOCKROOM_NOW` set to the time the run started (`overview.md` 4), and its
own empty temporary directory (`TMPDIR`), removed after the run.

2.4 The header of a run names the run id, the runner and the release under
test, and prints a replay line that repeats the run with the same seed, hash
seed, timezone and clock:

    python tools/ci.py --seed 551204 --hash-seed 2871120944 --tz America/Los_Angeles --now 2027-01-29T18:04:11Z

`--order sorted` and `--order reverse` replace the shuffle. `-k TEXT` keeps
the tests whose id contains `TEXT` (several `-k` may be given) and runs them
in the order they have in the full run. `--list` prints the order and runs
nothing. Run `python tools/ci.py --help` for the rest.

2.5 Each test prints one line, `ok`, `FAIL`, `ERROR` or `skip`, with its id.
After the last test the runner prints a `---- FAIL:` or `---- ERROR:` block
with the traceback of each test that did not pass, then a `result:` line. A
run cancelled by an operator (Ctrl-C, or a cancel in the CI interface) stops
in the test that was running; that test is reported as an `ERROR` ending in
`KeyboardInterrupt`, and the last line reads `run cancelled after ...`.

## 3. CI logs

3.1 The output of recent CI runs is kept in `logs/ci/`, one file per run,
named `YYYY-MM-DD-run-ID.log` after the start date (UTC) and the run id.

3.2 The logs are the runner's output as it was printed; nothing is added or
removed.

## 4. Triage of intermittent failures

4.1 A test that fails in some runs and passes in others is intermittent. The
cause is a defect in the package or in the test, not bad luck. Before a
failure is filed, it is traced to its root cause: the line of code that is
wrong.

4.2 One root cause can fail several tests, and one test can fail for more
than one root cause (in different runs). A failure that does not come from a
defect in the current code is not filed.

4.3 Each root cause is filed under one of these classes:

| Class | The result depends on |
|---|---|
| `shared-state` | a module-level or class-level mutable object (not a cache) that one call changes and a later call reads |
| `cache-key` | a cache whose key leaves out part of the input, so a call gets a result stored for different input |
| `hash-order` | the iteration order of a set or frozenset, which changes with `PYTHONHASHSEED` |
| `clock` | the current date or time, in the same way in every timezone |
| `timezone` | the local timezone of the process |
| `temp-file` | a file path outside the caller's own directory that two writers, or a writer and a file left behind, can share |
| `float-rounding` | binary floating point where decimal arithmetic is needed |
| `thread-race` | the timing of threads or processes running at the same time |
| `resource` | the speed, memory or disk of the machine |
| `network` | a network service or name lookup |

4.4 Fixes go into the package. A test is changed only when the test itself is
wrong; editing a test so that it no longer hits a defect hides the defect.

4.1 A test that fails in some runs and passes in others is intermittent. The
cause is a defect in the package or in the test, not bad luck. Before a
failure is filed, it is traced to its root cause: the line of code that is
wrong.

4.2 One root cause can fail several tests, and one test can fail for more
than one root cause (in different runs). A failure that does not come from a
defect in the current code is not filed.

4.3 Each root cause is filed under one of these classes:

| Class | The result depends on |
|---|---|
| `shared-state` | a module-level or class-level mutable object (not a cache) that one call changes and a later call reads |
| `cache-key` | a cache whose key leaves out part of the input, so a call gets a result stored for different input |
| `hash-order` | the iteration order of a set or frozenset, which changes with `PYTHONHASHSEED` |
| `clock` | the current date or time, in the same way in every timezone |
| `timezone` | the local timezone of the process |
| `temp-file` | a file path outside the caller's own directory that two writers, or a writer and a file left behind, can share |
| `float-rounding` | binary floating point where decimal arithmetic is needed |
| `thread-race` | the timing of threads or processes running at the same time |
| `resource` | the speed, memory or disk of the machine |
| `network` | a network service or name lookup |

4.4 Fixes go into the package. A test is changed only when the test itself is
wrong; editing a test so that it no longer hits a defect hides the defect.

# stockroom: overview

`stockroom` keeps stock for small warehouses: the item catalog, the bin
layout and where incoming pallets go, stock movements by lot, reorder
suggestions and review dates, freight quotes from carrier rate tables, and
the CSV reports built from all of these. It is a library; callers build the
objects and call the functions. It uses only the Python standard library.

| Note | Covers |
|---|---|
| `settings.md` | the settings table, overrides, units and rounding |
| `catalog.md` | item records and the catalog |
| `bins.md` | bin codes, the layout, walking cost, putaway |
| `stock.md` | the ledger, lots, aging, reorder points, review dates |
| `rates.md` | carrier rate tables, quotes, the table cache |
| `exports.md` | CSV exports and the standard files |
| `testing.md` | the unit tests, the CI runner, its logs, triage of failures |
| `changelog.md` | what changed between releases |

## 1. Modules

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `stockroom.clock` | the current time and the business date |
| `stockroom.settings` | built-in settings and overrides |
| `stockroom.units` | weights and lengths |
| `stockroom.catalog` | items |
| `stockroom.bins` | bins, layout, putaway |
| `stockroom.ledger` | movements and lots |
| `stockroom.reorder` | demand, reorder points, suggestions, reviews |
| `stockroom.rates` | rate tables and quotes |
| `stockroom.export` | CSV report files |
| `stockroom.reports` | the standard reports |
| `stockroom.errors` | the error classes |

## 2. Conventions

2.1 Weights are whole grams and lengths whole millimetres inside the package.
Other units appear only where a value is shown or read (`settings.md` 3).

2.2 Money is whole cents of the currency of the rate table it comes from.

2.3 Every error the package raises on purpose is a subclass of
`stockroom.errors.StockroomError`. Callers may rely on the subclass; messages
are for people and may change.

2.4 A function returns the same result for the same arguments, the same
settings and the same current time, whatever was called before it in the same
process, whatever the order of the calls, and whatever the process
environment holds besides `STOCKROOM_NOW` (section 4). In particular results
do not depend on `PYTHONHASHSEED`, on the timezone of the process (`TZ`) or on
files left in the temporary directory by earlier calls.

2.5 The package never changes process-wide state that it does not own: it
does not set environment variables, change the working directory, change the
process timezone or install signal handlers.

## 3. Dates

3.1 Every date the package stores or prints is a calendar date in UTC. The
**business date** is the UTC date of the current time: a call made at
2027-03-14T23:30Z belongs to 2027-03-14 everywhere in the world, and one made
at 2027-03-15T00:10Z to 2027-03-15.

3.2 Functions that take an optional date (`as_of`, `on`, `last`) use the
business date when it is left out.

3.3 Dates are written `YYYY-MM-DD`. Times are ISO 8601 with a `Z` or an
offset; a time without one is refused.

## 4. The current time

4.1 `stockroom.clock.now()` is the only source of the current time in the
package. It returns an aware datetime in UTC.

4.2 When the environment variable `STOCKROOM_NOW` holds an ISO 8601 time with
a `Z` or an offset, `now()` returns that time (converted to UTC) for the whole
process. The CI runner sets it for every run (`testing.md` 2.3), so a run can
be repeated with the same clock.

4.3 `stockroom.clock.today()` returns the business date (3.1).

## 5. Versions

The release is `stockroom.__version__`. The changelog lists the changes of
each release.

# stockroom: overview

`stockroom` keeps stock for small warehouses: the item catalog, the bin
layout and where incoming pallets go, stock movements by lot, reorder
suggestions and review dates, freight quotes from carrier rate tables, and
the CSV reports built from all of these. It is a library; callers build the
objects and call the functions. It uses only the Python standard library.

| Note | Covers |
|---|---|
| `settings.md` | the settings table, overrides, units and rounding |
| `catalog.md` | item records and the catalog |
| `bins.md` | bin codes, the layout, walking cost, putaway |
| `stock.md` | the ledger, lots, aging, reorder points, review dates |
| `rates.md` | carrier rate tables, quotes, the table cache |
| `exports.md` | CSV exports and the standard files |
| `testing.md` | the unit tests, the CI runner, its logs, triage of failures |
| `changelog.md` | what changed between releases |

## 1. Modules

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `stockroom.clock` | the current time and the business date |
| `stockroom.settings` | built-in settings and overrides |
| `stockroom.units` | weights and lengths |
| `stockroom.catalog` | items |
| `stockroom.bins` | bins, layout, putaway |
| `stockroom.ledger` | movements and lots |
| `stockroom.reorder` | demand, reorder points, suggestions, reviews |
| `stockroom.rates` | rate tables and quotes |
| `stockroom.export` | CSV report files |
| `stockroom.reports` | the standard reports |
| `stockroom.errors` | the error classes |

## 2. Conventions

2.1 Weights are whole grams and lengths whole millimetres inside the package.
Other units appear only where a value is shown or read (`settings.md` 3).

2.2 Money is whole cents of the currency of the rate table it comes from.

2.3 Every error the package raises on purpose is a subclass of
`stockroom.errors.StockroomError`. Callers may rely on the subclass; messages
are for people and may change.

2.4 A function returns the same result for the same arguments, the same
settings and the same current time, whatever was called before it in the same
process, whatever the order of the calls, and whatever the process
environment holds besides `STOCKROOM_NOW` (section 4). In particular results
do not depend on `PYTHONHASHSEED`, on the timezone of the process (`TZ`) or on
files left in the temporary directory by earlier calls.

2.5 The package never changes process-wide state that it does not own: it
does not set environment variables, change the working directory, change the
process timezone or install signal handlers.

## 3. Dates

3.1 Every date the package stores or prints is a calendar date in UTC. The
**business date** is the UTC date of the current time: a call made at
2027-03-14T23:30Z belongs to 2027-03-14 everywhere in the world, and one made
at 2027-03-15T00:10Z to 2027-03-15.

3.2 Functions that take an optional date (`as_of`, `on`, `last`) use the
business date when it is left out.

3.3 Dates are written `YYYY-MM-DD`. Times are ISO 8601 with a `Z` or an
offset; a time without one is refused.

## 4. The current time

4.1 `stockroom.clock.now()` is the only source of the current time in the
package. It returns an aware datetime in UTC.

4.2 When the environment variable `STOCKROOM_NOW` holds an ISO 8601 time with
a `Z` or an offset, `now()` returns that time (converted to UTC) for the whole
process. The CI runner sets it for every run (`testing.md` 2.3), so a run can
be repeated with the same clock.

4.3 `stockroom.clock.today()` returns the business date (3.1).

## 5. Versions

The release is `stockroom.__version__`. The changelog lists the changes of
each release.

    14	def parse_code(code: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    15	    """(aisle, bay, level) of a bin code such as C-07-2; aisle A is 0."""
    16	    m = CODE.match(code) if isinstance(code, str) else None
    17	    if not m:
    18	        raise BinError(f"bad bin code {code!r}")
    19	    bay = int(m.group(2))
    20	    if bay == 0:
    21	        raise BinError(f"bad bin code {code!r}: bays start at 01")
    22	    return ord(m.group(1)) - ord("A"), bay, int(m.group(3))

    25	def distance(origin: str, code: str) -> int:
    26	    """Walking cost from origin to a bin (bins.md 3.1)."""
    27	    a1, b1, _ = parse_code(origin)
    28	    a2, b2, level = parse_code(code)
    29	    return 4 * abs(a1 - a2) + 2 * abs(b1 - b2) + 3 * (level - 1)

    32	@dataclass(frozen=True)

    34	    code: str
    35	    dims_mm: tuple[int, int, int]
    36	    max_kg: int
    37	    zones: frozenset

    39	    def fits(self, item: Item, qty: int, max_fill: float) -> bool:
    40	        if item.weight_g * qty > self.max_kg * 1000:
    41	            return False
    42	        if any(i > b for i, b in zip(sorted(item.dims_mm), sorted(self.dims_mm))):
    43	            return False
    44	        l, w, h = item.dims_mm
    45	        bl, bw, bh = self.dims_mm
    46	        return l * w * h * qty <= bl * bw * bh * max_fill

    51	        self._bins: dict[str, Bin] = {}

    55	    def add(self, b: Bin) -> None:
    56	        parse_code(b.code)
    57	        old = self._bins.get(b.code)
    58	        if old is None:
    59	            self._bins[b.code] = b
    60	        elif (old.dims_mm, old.max_kg) != (b.dims_mm, b.max_kg):
    61	            raise BinError(f"bin {b.code} is listed twice with different sizes")
    62	        else:
    63	            self._bins[b.code] = Bin(b.code, b.dims_mm, b.max_kg, old.zones | b.zones)

    78	        return [b for b in self._bins.values() if zone in b.zones]

    82	        out = cls()

    98	def choose_bin(item: Item, layout: Layout, settings: dict, qty: int = 1, occupied=frozenset()) -> str:
    99	    """The bin a pallet of qty units of item goes to (bins.md 3)."""
   100	    origin = settings["putaway"]["origin"]
   101	    max_fill = settings["putaway"]["max_fill"]
   102	    pool = layout.in_zone(item.zone) if item.zone else list(layout)
   103	    candidates = {b.code for b in pool if b.code not in occupied and b.fits(item, qty, max_fill)}
   104	    if not candidates:
   105	        raise NoBinError(f"no free bin for {qty} x {item.sku}")
   106	    return min(candidates, key=lambda code: distance(origin, code))
   107	
   108	
   109	def putaway(lines, catalog, layout: Layout, settings: dict, occupied=()) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
   110	    """Bins for the pallets of a receipt, in receipt order: (sku, qty, bin) per pallet.
   111	
   112	    A line of n units becomes ceil(n / case_qty) pallets of at most case_qty
   113	    units; each pallet takes its own bin.
   114	    """
   115	    taken = set(occupied)
   116	    plan = []
   117	    for sku, qty in lines:
   118	        item = catalog.get(sku)
   119	        left = qty
   120	        while left > 0:
   121	            n = min(left, item.case_qty)
   122	            code = choose_bin(item, layout, settings, n, frozenset(taken))
   123	            taken.add(code)
   124	            plan.append((sku, n, code))
   125	            left -= n
   126	    return plan

    52	        if qty <= 0:

    55	        lots = self._lots.setdefault((site, sku), [])
    56	        if any(l[0] == lot for l in lots):
    57	            raise LedgerError(f"lot {lot} of {sku} is already in stock at {site}")

    70	            n = min(qty, lot[2])

    61	        out.append(Suggestion(item.sku, have, point, cases * item.case_qty, review))

    11	CODE = re.compile(r"^([A-Z])-(\d{2})-([1-9])$")

    13	
    14	def parse_code(code: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    15	    """(aisle, bay, level) of a bin code such as C-07-2; aisle A is 0."""
    16	    m = CODE.match(code) if isinstance(code, str) else None
    17	    if not m:
    18	        raise BinError(f"bad bin code {code!r}")
    19	    bay = int(m.group(2))
    20	    if bay == 0:
    21	        raise BinError(f"bad bin code {code!r}: bays start at 01")
    22	    return ord(m.group(1)) - ord("A"), bay, int(m.group(3))
    23	
    24	
    25	def distance(origin: str, code: str) -> int:
    26	    """Walking cost from origin to a bin (bins.md 3.1)."""
    27	    a1, b1, _ = parse_code(origin)
    28	    a2, b2, level = parse_code(code)
    29	    return 4 * abs(a1 - a2) + 2 * abs(b1 - b2) + 3 * (level - 1)

    32	@dataclass(frozen=True)

    34	    code: str
    35	    dims_mm: tuple[int, int, int]
    36	    max_kg: int

    40	        if item.weight_g * qty > self.max_kg * 1000:
    41	            return False
    42	        if any(i > b for i, b in zip(sorted(item.dims_mm), sorted(self.dims_mm))):
    43	            return False
    44	        l, w, h = item.dims_mm

    46	        return l * w * h * qty <= bl * bw * bh * max_fill

    56	        parse_code(b.code)
    57	        old = self._bins.get(b.code)
    58	        if old is None:

    60	        elif (old.dims_mm, old.max_kg) != (b.dims_mm, b.max_kg):
    61	            raise BinError(f"bin {b.code} is listed twice with different sizes")
    62	        else:

    98	def choose_bin(item: Item, layout: Layout, settings: dict, qty: int = 1, occupied=frozenset()) -> str:
    99	    """The bin a pallet of qty units of item goes to (bins.md 3)."""
   100	    origin = settings["putaway"]["origin"]
   101	    max_fill = settings["putaway"]["max_fill"]
   102	    pool = layout.in_zone(item.zone) if item.zone else list(layout)
   103	    candidates = {b.code for b in pool if b.code not in occupied and b.fits(item, qty, max_fill)}
   104	    if not candidates:
   105	        raise NoBinError(f"no free bin for {qty} x {item.sku}")
   106	    return min(candidates, key=lambda code: distance(origin, code))
   107	
   108	
   109	def putaway(lines, catalog, layout: Layout, settings: dict, occupied=()) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
   110	    """Bins for the pallets of a receipt, in receipt order: (sku, qty, bin) per pallet.
   111	
   112	    A line of n units becomes ceil(n / case_qty) pallets of at most case_qty
   113	    units; each pallet takes its own bin.
   114	    """
   115	    taken = set(occupied)
   116	    plan = []
   117	    for sku, qty in lines:
   118	        item = catalog.get(sku)
   119	        left = qty
   120	        while left > 0:
   121	            n = min(left, item.case_qty)
   122	            code = choose_bin(item, layout, settings, n, frozenset(taken))
   123	            taken.add(code)
   124	            plan.append((sku, n, code))
   125	            left -= n
   126	    return plan

   116	    plan = []

   110	    """Bins for the pallets of a receipt, in receipt order: (sku, qty, bin) per pallet.
   111	
   112	    A line of n units becomes ceil(n / case_qty) pallets of at most case_qty
   113	    units; each pallet takes its own bin.
   114	    """
   115	    taken = set(occupied)
   116	    plan = []
   117	    for sku, qty in lines:
   118	        item = catalog.get(sku)
   119	        left = qty
   120	        while left > 0:
   121	            n = min(left, item.case_qty)
   122	            code = choose_bin(item, layout, settings, n, frozenset(taken))
   123	            taken.add(code)
   124	            plan.append((sku, n, code))
   125	            left -= n
   126	    return plan

   112	    kg = weight_g / 1000

    21	
    22	        with ReportWriter(path, ["sku", "qty"]) as w:

    31	        self.rows = 0

    34	        self._spool = None

    36	    def __enter__(self):

    38	            raise ReportError(f"no directory {self.target.parent}")
    39	        spool = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "stockroom-spool"
    40	        spool.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    41	        self._spool = spool / f"{self.target.name}.part"
    42	        self._fh = open(self._spool, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    43	        self._writer = csv.writer(self._fh, lineterminator="\n")
    44	        self._writer.writerow(self.columns)
    45	        return self

    48	        values = list(values)
    49	        if len(values) != len(self.columns):
    50	            raise ReportError(f"row {self.rows + 1} has {len(values)} cells, the report has {len(self.columns)} columns")
    51	        self._writer.writerow([_cell(v) for v in values])
    52	        self.rows += 1

    24	    """Mean units issued per day over the demand_days days that end on as_of."""
    25	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    26	    days = settings["reorder"]["demand_days"]
    27	    if days <= 0:

    29	    issued = ledger.issued(sku, as_of - timedelta(days=days - 1), as_of, site)

    38	    """The review after the one on last (stock.md 6)."""
    39	    last = last or clock.today()
    40	    day = ((settings or {}).get("reorder") or {}).get("review_day") or last.day
    41	    if not isinstance(day, int) or not 1 <= day <= 31:

    49	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    50	    review = next_review(as_of, settings)
    51	    out = []
    52	    for item in catalog:

    54	        point = reorder_point(demand, item.lead_days, settings)
    55	        have = ledger.on_hand(item.sku, site)

    58	        cover = math.ceil(demand * (review - as_of).days)

    35	def _decimal(value, what: str) -> Decimal:
    36	    try:
    37	        d = Decimal(str(value))
    38	    except InvalidOperation:
    39	        raise RateError(f"{what} is not a number: {value!r}") from None
    40	    if not d.is_finite() or d < 0:
    41	        raise RateError(f"{what} must be a number of at least 0")

    45	def parse(spec: dict) -> RateTable:
    46	    if not isinstance(spec, dict):
    47	        raise RateError("a rate table is a JSON object")
    48	    for key in ("carrier", "service", "effective", "currency", "bands", "zones"):
    49	        if key not in spec:
    50	            raise RateError(f"rate table without {key}")
    51	    try:
    52	        parse_date(spec["effective"])
    53	    except ValueError as e:
    54	        raise RateError(f"effective: {e}") from None
    55	    bands = []
    56	    for b in spec["bands"]:
    57	        try:
    58	            up_to, cents = int(b["up_to_kg"]), int(b["cents"])
    59	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
    60	            raise RateError(f"bad band {b!r}") from None
    61	        if bands and up_to <= bands[-1][0]:
    62	            raise RateError("bands must rise in up_to_kg")
    63	        if up_to <= 0 or cents < 0:
    64	            raise RateError(f"bad band {b!r}")
    65	        bands.append((up_to, cents))
    66	    if not bands:
    67	        raise RateError("a rate table needs at least one band")
    68	    zones = {str(z): _decimal(f, f"zone {z}") for z, f in spec["zones"].items()}
    69	    if not zones:
    70	        raise RateError("a rate table needs at least one zone")
    71	    return RateTable(
    72	        carrier=str(spec["carrier"]),
    73	        service=str(spec["service"]),
    74	        effective=spec["effective"],
    75	        currency=str(spec["currency"]),
    76	        bands=tuple(bands),
    77	        over_per_kg=int(spec.get("over_per_kg_cents", 0)),
    78	        zones=zones,
    79	        fuel=_decimal(spec.get("fuel_pct", 0), "fuel_pct"),
    80	    )

    82	
    83	def table(spec: dict) -> RateTable:
    84	    """The parsed table for spec; each distinct table is parsed once (rates.md 4)."""
    85	    try:
    86	        key = (spec["carrier"], spec["service"], spec["effective"])
    87	    except (KeyError, TypeError):
    88	        raise RateError("a rate table needs carrier, service and effective") from None
    89	    cached = _tables.get(key)
    90	    if cached is not None:
    91	        _stats["hits"] += 1
    92	        return cached
    93	    _stats["misses"] += 1
    94	    parsed = parse(spec)
    95	    _tables[key] = parsed
    96	    return parsed

    99	def cache_stats() -> dict:
   100	    return {"tables": len(_tables), **_stats}
   101	
   102	
   103	def clear_cache() -> None:
   104	    _tables.clear()
   105	    _stats.update(hits=0, misses=0)

   108	def billable_kg(weight_g: int, dims_mm=None) -> int:
   109	    """Whole kilograms billed: the actual or the volume weight, whichever is more."""
   110	    if weight_g <= 0:
   111	        raise RateError("weight must be above 0")
   112	    kg = weight_g / 1000
   113	    if dims_mm is not None:
   114	        l, w, h = dims_mm
   115	        kg = max(kg, (l * w * h / 1000) / VOLUME_DIVISOR)
   116	    return max(1, math.ceil(kg))
   117	
   118	
   119	def quote(spec: dict, weight_g: int, zone, dims_mm=None) -> int:
   120	    """Price in cents of one parcel (rates.md 3)."""
   121	    t = table(spec)
   122	    kg = billable_kg(weight_g, dims_mm)
   123	    for up_to, cents in t.bands:
   124	        if kg <= up_to:
   125	            base = Decimal(cents)
   126	            break
   127	    else:
   128	        last_up_to, last_cents = t.bands[-1]
   129	        base = Decimal(last_cents + (kg - last_up_to) * t.over_per_kg)
   130	    price = base * t.zone_factor(zone) * (1 + t.fuel / 100)
   131	    return int(price.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN))

   135	    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
   136	    return f"{sign}{abs(cents) // 100}.{abs(cents) % 100:02d} {currency}"

    19	class ReportWriter:
    20	    """Writes one CSV report. Use it as a context manager:
    21	
    22	        with ReportWriter(path, ["sku", "qty"]) as w:
    23	            w.row(["ABC-0001", 4])
    24	    """
    25	
    26	    def __init__(self, target, columns):
    27	        self.target = Path(target)
    28	        self.columns = list(columns)
    29	        if not self.columns or len(set(self.columns)) != len(self.columns):
    30	            raise ReportError("a report needs distinct column names")
    31	        self.rows = 0
    32	        self._fh = None
    33	        self._writer = None
    34	        self._spool = None
    35	
    36	    def __enter__(self):
    37	        if not self.target.parent.is_dir():
    38	            raise ReportError(f"no directory {self.target.parent}")
    39	        spool = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "stockroom-spool"
    40	        spool.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    41	        self._spool = spool / f"{self.target.name}.part"
    42	        self._fh = open(self._spool, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    43	        self._writer = csv.writer(self._fh, lineterminator="\n")
    44	        self._writer.writerow(self.columns)
    45	        return self
    46	
    47	    def row(self, values) -> None:
    48	        values = list(values)
    49	        if len(values) != len(self.columns):
    50	            raise ReportError(f"row {self.rows + 1} has {len(values)} cells, the report has {len(self.columns)} columns")
    51	        self._writer.writerow([_cell(v) for v in values])
    52	        self.rows += 1
    53	
    54	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
    55	        self._fh.close()
    56	        if exc_type is None:
    57	            os.replace(self._spool, self.target)
    58	        return False
    59	
    60	
    61	def write_report(target, columns, rows) -> int:
    62	    with ReportWriter(target, columns) as w:
    63	        for r in rows:
    64	            w.row(r)
    65	    return w.rows

    86	        """A count correction on one lot; a lot that reaches 0 leaves the stock."""
    87	        on = self._date(on)
    88	        lots = self._lots.get((site, sku), [])

   101	        if to_site == site:
   102	            raise LedgerError("a transfer needs two different sites")

   104	        taken = self._take(site, sku, qty)

   108	            if same:

   110	            else:
   111	                dest.append([lot, received, n])

    23	def daily_demand(ledger: Ledger, sku: str, settings: dict, as_of: date | None = None, site: str = "main") -> Decimal:
    24	    """Mean units issued per day over the demand_days days that end on as_of."""
    25	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    26	    days = settings["reorder"]["demand_days"]
    27	    if days <= 0:
    28	        raise SettingsError("reorder.demand_days must be at least 1")
    29	    issued = ledger.issued(sku, as_of - timedelta(days=days - 1), as_of, site)
    30	    return (Decimal(issued) / days).quantize(Decimal("0.0001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)

    34	    return math.ceil(demand * (lead_days + settings["reorder"]["safety_days"]))

    37	def next_review(last: date | None = None, settings: dict | None = None) -> date:
    38	    """The review after the one on last (stock.md 6)."""
    39	    last = last or clock.today()
    40	    day = ((settings or {}).get("reorder") or {}).get("review_day") or last.day
    41	    if not isinstance(day, int) or not 1 <= day <= 31:
    42	        raise SettingsError("reorder.review_day must be a day of the month")
    43	    y, m = (last.year + 1, 1) if last.month == 12 else (last.year, last.month + 1)

    47	def suggestions(ledger: Ledger, catalog: Catalog, settings: dict, as_of: date | None = None, site: str = "main") -> list[Suggestion]:
    48	    """One suggestion per item whose stock is at or below its reorder point, by sku."""
    49	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    50	    review = next_review(as_of, settings)
    51	    out = []
    52	    for item in catalog:
    53	        demand = daily_demand(ledger, item.sku, settings, as_of, site)
    54	        point = reorder_point(demand, item.lead_days, settings)
    55	        have = ledger.on_hand(item.sku, site)
    56	        if point == 0 or have > point:
    57	            continue
    58	        cover = math.ceil(demand * (review - as_of).days)
    59	        want = point + cover - have
    60	        cases = max(1, math.ceil(want / item.case_qty))
    61	        out.append(Suggestion(item.sku, have, point, cases * item.case_qty, review))

    13	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    14	class RateTable:
    15	    carrier: str
    16	    service: str
    17	    effective: str
    18	    currency: str
    19	    bands: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
    20	    over_per_kg: int
    21	    zones: dict

    24	    def zone_factor(self, zone: str) -> Decimal:
    25	        try:
    26	            return self.zones[str(zone)]
    27	        except KeyError:
    28	            raise RateError(f"{self.carrier} {self.service}: no zone {zone}") from None
    29	
    30	
    31	_tables: dict = {}
    32	_stats = {"hits": 0, "misses": 0}
    33	
    34	
    35	def _decimal(value, what: str) -> Decimal:
    36	    try:
    37	        d = Decimal(str(value))
    38	    except InvalidOperation:
    39	        raise RateError(f"{what} is not a number: {value!r}") from None
    40	    if not d.is_finite() or d < 0:
    41	        raise RateError(f"{what} must be a number of at least 0")
    42	    return d
    43	
    44	
    45	def parse(spec: dict) -> RateTable:
    46	    if not isinstance(spec, dict):
    47	        raise RateError("a rate table is a JSON object")
    48	    for key in ("carrier", "service", "effective", "currency", "bands", "zones"):
    49	        if key not in spec:
    50	            raise RateError(f"rate table without {key}")
    51	    try:
    52	        parse_date(spec["effective"])
    53	    except ValueError as e:
    54	        raise RateError(f"effective: {e}") from None
    55	    bands = []
    56	    for b in spec["bands"]:
    57	        try:
    58	            up_to, cents = int(b["up_to_kg"]), int(b["cents"])
    59	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
    60	            raise RateError(f"bad band {b!r}") from None
    61	        if bands and up_to <= bands[-1][0]:
    62	            raise RateError("bands must rise in up_to_kg")
    63	        if up_to <= 0 or cents < 0:
    64	            raise RateError(f"bad band {b!r}")
    65	        bands.append((up_to, cents))
    66	    if not bands:
    67	        raise RateError("a rate table needs at least one band")
    68	    zones = {str(z): _decimal(f, f"zone {z}") for z, f in spec["zones"].items()}
    69	    if not zones:
    70	        raise RateError("a rate table needs at least one zone")
    71	    return RateTable(
    72	        carrier=str(spec["carrier"]),
    73	        service=str(spec["service"]),
    74	        effective=spec["effective"],
    75	        currency=str(spec["currency"]),
    76	        bands=tuple(bands),
    77	        over_per_kg=int(spec.get("over_per_kg_cents", 0)),
    78	        zones=zones,
    79	        fuel=_decimal(spec.get("fuel_pct", 0), "fuel_pct"),
    80	    )
    81	
    82	
    83	def table(spec: dict) -> RateTable:
    84	    """The parsed table for spec; each distinct table is parsed once (rates.md 4)."""
    85	    try:
    86	        key = (spec["carrier"], spec["service"], spec["effective"])
    87	    except (KeyError, TypeError):
    88	        raise RateError("a rate table needs carrier, service and effective") from None
    89	    cached = _tables.get(key)
    90	    if cached is not None:
    91	        _stats["hits"] += 1
    92	        return cached
    93	    _stats["misses"] += 1
    94	    parsed = parse(spec)
    95	    _tables[key] = parsed
    96	    return parsed
    97	
    98	
    99	def cache_stats() -> dict:
   100	    return {"tables": len(_tables), **_stats}
   101	
   102	
   103	def clear_cache() -> None:
   104	    _tables.clear()
   105	    _stats.update(hits=0, misses=0)

   107	
   108	def billable_kg(weight_g: int, dims_mm=None) -> int:
   109	    """Whole kilograms billed: the actual or the volume weight, whichever is more."""
   110	    if weight_g <= 0:
   111	        raise RateError("weight must be above 0")
   112	    kg = weight_g / 1000
   113	    if dims_mm is not None:
   114	        l, w, h = dims_mm
   115	        kg = max(kg, (l * w * h / 1000) / VOLUME_DIVISOR)
   116	    return max(1, math.ceil(kg))
   117	
   118	
   119	def quote(spec: dict, weight_g: int, zone, dims_mm=None) -> int:
   120	    """Price in cents of one parcel (rates.md 3)."""
   121	    t = table(spec)
   122	    kg = billable_kg(weight_g, dims_mm)
   123	    for up_to, cents in t.bands:
   124	        if kg <= up_to:
   125	            base = Decimal(cents)
   126	            break
   127	    else:
   128	        last_up_to, last_cents = t.bands[-1]
   129	        base = Decimal(last_cents + (kg - last_up_to) * t.over_per_kg)
   130	    price = base * t.zone_factor(zone) * (1 + t.fuel / 100)
   131	    return int(price.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN))
   132	
   133	
   134	def format_cents(cents: int, currency: str) -> str:
   135	    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
   136	    return f"{sign}{abs(cents) // 100}.{abs(cents) % 100:02d} {currency}"

    19	class ReportWriter:
    20	    """Writes one CSV report. Use it as a context manager:
    21	
    22	        with ReportWriter(path, ["sku", "qty"]) as w:
    23	            w.row(["ABC-0001", 4])
    24	    """
    25	
    26	    def __init__(self, target, columns):
    27	        self.target = Path(target)
    28	        self.columns = list(columns)
    29	        if not self.columns or len(set(self.columns)) != len(self.columns):
    30	            raise ReportError("a report needs distinct column names")
    31	        self.rows = 0
    32	        self._fh = None
    33	        self._writer = None
    34	        self._spool = None
    35	
    36	    def __enter__(self):
    37	        if not self.target.parent.is_dir():
    38	            raise ReportError(f"no directory {self.target.parent}")
    39	        spool = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "stockroom-spool"
    40	        spool.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    41	        self._spool = spool / f"{self.target.name}.part"
    42	        self._fh = open(self._spool, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    43	        self._writer = csv.writer(self._fh, lineterminator="\n")
    44	        self._writer.writerow(self.columns)
    45	        return self
    46	
    47	    def row(self, values) -> None:
    48	        values = list(values)
    49	        if len(values) != len(self.columns):
    50	            raise ReportError(f"row {self.rows + 1} has {len(values)} cells, the report has {len(self.columns)} columns")
    51	        self._writer.writerow([_cell(v) for v in values])
    52	        self.rows += 1
    53	
    54	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
    55	        self._fh.close()
    56	        if exc_type is None:
    57	            os.replace(self._spool, self.target)
    58	        return False
    59	
    60	
    61	def write_report(target, columns, rows) -> int:
    62	    with ReportWriter(target, columns) as w:
    63	        for r in rows:
    64	            w.row(r)
    65	    return w.rows

    69	    try:

    71	            data = list(csv.reader(fh))
    72	    except OSError as e:

    74	    if not data:
    75	        raise ReportError(f"{path} is empty")
    76	    return data[0], data[1:]

    23	def daily_demand(ledger: Ledger, sku: str, settings: dict, as_of: date | None = None, site: str = "main") -> Decimal:
    24	    """Mean units issued per day over the demand_days days that end on as_of."""
    25	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    26	    days = settings["reorder"]["demand_days"]
    27	    if days <= 0:
    28	        raise SettingsError("reorder.demand_days must be at least 1")
    29	    issued = ledger.issued(sku, as_of - timedelta(days=days - 1), as_of, site)
    30	    return (Decimal(issued) / days).quantize(Decimal("0.0001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)

    34	    return math.ceil(demand * (lead_days + settings["reorder"]["safety_days"]))

    37	def next_review(last: date | None = None, settings: dict | None = None) -> date:
    38	    """The review after the one on last (stock.md 6)."""
    39	    last = last or clock.today()
    40	    day = ((settings or {}).get("reorder") or {}).get("review_day") or last.day
    41	    if not isinstance(day, int) or not 1 <= day <= 31:
    42	        raise SettingsError("reorder.review_day must be a day of the month")
    43	    y, m = (last.year + 1, 1) if last.month == 12 else (last.year, last.month + 1)
    44	    return date(y, m, day)

    48	    """One suggestion per item whose stock is at or below its reorder point, by sku."""
    49	    as_of = as_of or clock.today()
    50	    review = next_review(as_of, settings)
    51	    out = []
    52	    for item in catalog:
    53	        demand = daily_demand(ledger, item.sku, settings, as_of, site)
    54	        point = reorder_point(demand, item.lead_days, settings)
    55	        have = ledger.on_hand(item.sku, site)
    56	        if point == 0 or have > point:
    57	            continue
    58	        cover = math.ceil(demand * (review - as_of).days)
    59	        want = point + cover - have
    60	        cases = max(1, math.ceil(want / item.case_qty))
    61	        out.append(Suggestion(item.sku, have, point, cases * item.case_qty, review))

# Bins and putaway

## 1. Bin codes

1.1 A bin code is an aisle letter, a two-digit bay and a one-digit level,
joined by hyphens: `C-07-2` is aisle C, bay 7, level 2. Bays start at `01`
and levels at `1` (the floor). Anything else raises `BinError`.

1.2 `parse_code` gives `(aisle, bay, level)` with aisle A as 0.

## 2. The layout

2.1 A layout is a list of bin records: `code`, `dims_mm` (inner length, width
and height in millimetres), `max_kg` (load limit in whole kilograms) and
`zones` (default `["ambient"]`).

2.2 A layout may list a bin more than once, for example once per zone it
belongs to. Records of one code are one bin: their zones are merged. Records
of one code with different sizes or load limits raise `BinError`.

2.3 An item with a `zone` may only go to bins of that zone. An item without a
zone may go to any bin.

## 3. Choosing a bin

3.1 The walking cost from the origin `putaway.origin` to a bin is

    4 x |aisle difference| + 2 x |bay difference| + 3 x (level - 1)

The origin's own level does not count.

3.2 A pallet of `qty` units fits a bin when its weight is within the load
limit, the item fits the bin in some orientation (sorted item dimensions each
at most the sorted bin dimensions), and `qty` times the item volume is at
most `putaway.max_fill` times the bin volume.

3.3 `choose_bin(item, layout, settings, qty, occupied)` returns the code of the
bin with the lowest walking cost among the bins that are allowed for the item
(2.3), not in `occupied`, and fit the pallet (3.2). When several bins have the
lowest cost, the bin with the smallest code wins, comparing codes as strings:
`A-04-1` before `B-02-1`. When no bin qualifies it raises `NoBinError`.

3.4 The result depends only on the layout's bins, the item, the quantity, the
occupied bins and the settings. The order in which the layout lists its bins
does not matter.

## 4. Putaway

4.1 `putaway(lines, catalog, layout, settings, occupied)` plans a receipt.
`lines` is a list of `(sku, qty)`. A line becomes pallets of `case_qty` units,
the last one holding what is left. Pallets are placed in receipt order, each
with `choose_bin`; a bin that receives a pallet is occupied for the pallets
after it.

4.2 The plan is a list of `(sku, qty, bin)`, one per pallet, in placement
order.
# Stock: ledger, lots, reorder

## 1. Movements

1.1 The ledger records movements in the order they happen. Each movement has
a sequence number (from 1), a kind, a sku, a signed quantity, a date and a
site (default `main`).

| Kind | Effect |
|---|---|
| `receipt` | adds a new lot with the received quantity |
| `issue` | takes units from the oldest lots first |
| `adjust` | changes the quantity of one named lot; a lot that reaches 0 is gone |
| `transfer` | moves units to another site, oldest lots first |

1.2 A movement dated before the last recorded movement raises `LedgerError`.
So does an issue or transfer of more units than the site holds, an
adjustment that would take a lot below 0, a receipt of a lot id the site
already holds for that sku, and a quantity of 0 or less where a positive one
is needed. A refused movement changes nothing.

1.3 A movement without a date is dated with the business date
(`overview.md` 3).

## 2. Lots

2.1 A lot keeps the date it was received. Lots are used oldest first (by
received date, then lot id). A transfer moves units lot by lot; the lots keep
their ids and received dates at the new site, and units of a lot id the new
site already holds are added to it.

2.2 `lots(sku, site)` lists the lots in stock, oldest first.
`on_hand(sku, site)` is the sum of their quantities.

## 3. Issued quantities

`issued(sku, since, until, site)` is the number of units issued from `since`
to `until`, both dates included. Transfers are not issues.

## 4. Aging

4.1 `aging(as_of, site)` lists every lot in stock as `(sku, lot, qty, age)`,
where age is the number of days from the received date to `as_of`. Without
`as_of` the business date is used.

4.2 Rows are sorted oldest first (highest age), then by sku, then by lot id.

## 5. Reorder points and suggestions

5.1 Daily demand is the number of units issued over the `reorder.demand_days`
days that end on the reference date (both ends included), divided by that
number of days, rounded half to even to 4 places.

5.2 The reorder point is daily demand times (lead days of the item plus
`reorder.safety_days`), rounded up to a whole unit.

5.3 `suggestions(ledger, catalog, settings, as_of, site)` gives one suggestion
per item, by sku, whose reorder point is above 0 and whose stock on hand is at
most the reorder point. A suggestion orders enough whole cases to reach the
reorder point plus the demand until the next review (daily demand times the
days from `as_of` to the next review, rounded up), and at least one case.

## 6. Review dates

6.1 Stock is reviewed once a month. `next_review(last, settings)` gives the
review after one held on `last` (the business date when left out).

6.2 The next review is in the month after `last`, on the same day of the
month as `last`, or on `reorder.review_day` when that is set. When the month
has no such day, the review is on its last day: after 2027-01-31 comes
2027-02-28, after 2028-01-30 comes 2028-02-29. After a review in December
comes one in January of the next year.

6.3 A `review_day` outside 1 to 31 raises `SettingsError`.
# Carrier rates

## 1. Rate tables

1.1 A carrier publishes a rate table per service as a JSON object:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `carrier`, `service` | names, as the carrier writes them |
| `effective` | first day the table applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `currency` | currency code of every amount |
| `bands` | list of `{"up_to_kg": n, "cents": c}`, `up_to_kg` rising |
| `over_per_kg_cents` | price of each kilogram above the last band (default 0) |
| `zones` | factor per destination zone, as strings: `{"1": "1.00", "2": "1.18"}` |
| `fuel_pct` | fuel surcharge in percent (default 0) |

1.2 A table that breaks 1.1 raises `RateError`: a missing field, no band, bands
that do not rise, a band with a weight of 0 or less or a negative price, no
zone, a factor or surcharge that is not a number of at least 0, a bad date.

1.3 Carriers reissue tables without changing `carrier`, `service` or
`effective`: a surcharge or a zone can change while the table keeps its
effective date. Two tables are the same table only when they are equal as
JSON values.

## 2. Billable weight

2.1 The billable weight of a parcel is the larger of its actual weight and
its volume weight (length x width x height in cubic centimetres divided by
5000), rounded up to a whole kilogram, and at least 1 kg.

2.2 A weight of 0 or less raises `RateError`.

## 3. Quotes

3.1 `quote(spec, weight_g, zone, dims_mm=None)` prices one parcel in cents:

1. take the price of the first band whose `up_to_kg` is at least the billable
   weight; above the last band, the last band's price plus
   `over_per_kg_cents` for each kilogram above it;
2. multiply by the zone factor and by `1 + fuel_pct / 100`;
3. round half to even to a whole cent, once, at the end.

3.2 A zone the table does not list raises `RateError`.

3.3 `format_cents(cents, currency)` writes `12.34 EUR`; a negative amount
gets a leading minus sign.

## 4. The table cache

4.1 Parsing a table is slow for large tables, so `table(spec)` keeps the
tables it has parsed for the life of the process. It parses a spec only when
it has not parsed an equal one before; otherwise it returns the table it
already has. `quote` uses `table`.

4.2 Specs are compared as JSON values (1.3): two specs with the same content
share one parsed table even when they are different objects or list their
keys in another order; specs that differ anywhere, in a band, a zone or the
surcharge, get their own tables. A spec that is changed after it was used is
compared by its new content when it is used again.

4.3 `cache_stats()` returns `{"tables": n, "hits": h, "misses": m}`: the

# Bins and putaway

## 1. Bin codes

1.1 A bin code is an aisle letter, a two-digit bay and a one-digit level,
joined by hyphens: `C-07-2` is aisle C, bay 7, level 2. Bays start at `01`
and levels at `1` (the floor). Anything else raises `BinError`.

1.2 `parse_code` gives `(aisle, bay, level)` with aisle A as 0.

## 2. The layout

2.1 A layout is a list of bin records: `code`, `dims_mm` (inner length, width
and height in millimetres), `max_kg` (load limit in whole kilograms) and
`zones` (default `["ambient"]`).

2.2 A layout may list a bin more than once, for example once per zone it
belongs to. Records of one code are one bin: their zones are merged. Records
of one code with different sizes or load limits raise `BinError`.

2.3 An item with a `zone` may only go to bins of that zone. An item without a
zone may go to any bin.

## 3. Choosing a bin

3.1 The walking cost from the origin `putaway.origin` to a bin is

    4 x |aisle difference| + 2 x |bay difference| + 3 x (level - 1)

The origin's own level does not count.

3.2 A pallet of `qty` units fits a bin when its weight is within the load
limit, the item fits the bin in some orientation (sorted item dimensions each
at most the sorted bin dimensions), and `qty` times the item volume is at
most `putaway.max_fill` times the bin volume.

3.3 `choose_bin(item, layout, settings, qty, occupied)` returns the code of the
bin with the lowest walking cost among the bins that are allowed for the item
(2.3), not in `occupied`, and fit the pallet (3.2). When several bins have the
lowest cost, the bin with the smallest code wins, comparing codes as strings:
`A-04-1` before `B-02-1`. When no bin qualifies it raises `NoBinError`.

3.4 The result depends only on the layout's bins, the item, the quantity, the
occupied bins and the settings. The order in which the layout lists its bins
does not matter.

## 4. Putaway

4.1 `putaway(lines, catalog, layout, settings, occupied)` plans a receipt.
`lines` is a list of `(sku, qty)`. A line becomes pallets of `case_qty` units,
the last one holding what is left. Pallets are placed in receipt order, each
with `choose_bin`; a bin that receives a pallet is occupied for the pallets
after it.

4.2 The plan is a list of `(sku, qty, bin)`, one per pallet, in placement
order.
# Stock: ledger, lots, reorder

## 1. Movements

1.1 The ledger records movements in the order they happen. Each movement has
a sequence number (from 1), a kind, a sku, a signed quantity, a date and a
site (default `main`).

| Kind | Effect |
|---|---|
| `receipt` | adds a new lot with the received quantity |
| `issue` | takes units from the oldest lots first |
| `adjust` | changes the quantity of one named lot; a lot that reaches 0 is gone |
| `transfer` | moves units to another site, oldest lots first |

1.2 A movement dated before the last recorded movement raises `LedgerError`.
So does an issue or transfer of more units than the site holds, an
adjustment that would take a lot below 0, a receipt of a lot id the site
already holds for that sku, and a quantity of 0 or less where a positive one
is needed. A refused movement changes nothing.

1.3 A movement without a date is dated with the business date
(`overview.md` 3).

## 2. Lots

2.1 A lot keeps the date it was received. Lots are used oldest first (by
received date, then lot id). A transfer moves units lot by lot; the lots keep
their ids and received dates at the new site, and units of a lot id the new
site already holds are added to it.

2.2 `lots(sku, site)` lists the lots in stock, oldest first.
`on_hand(sku, site)` is the sum of their quantities.

## 3. Issued quantities

`issued(sku, since, until, site)` is the number of units issued from `since`
to `until`, both dates included. Transfers are not issues.

## 4. Aging

4.1 `aging(as_of, site)` lists every lot in stock as `(sku, lot, qty, age)`,
where age is the number of days from the received date to `as_of`. Without
`as_of` the business date is used.

4.2 Rows are sorted oldest first (highest age), then by sku, then by lot id.

## 5. Reorder points and suggestions

5.1 Daily demand is the number of units issued over the `reorder.demand_days`
days that end on the reference date (both ends included), divided by that
number of days, rounded half to even to 4 places.

5.2 The reorder point is daily demand times (lead days of the item plus
`reorder.safety_days`), rounded up to a whole unit.

5.3 `suggestions(ledger, catalog, settings, as_of, site)` gives one suggestion
per item, by sku, whose reorder point is above 0 and whose stock on hand is at
most the reorder point. A suggestion orders enough whole cases to reach the
reorder point plus the demand until the next review (daily demand times the
days from `as_of` to the next review, rounded up), and at least one case.

## 6. Review dates

6.1 Stock is reviewed once a month. `next_review(last, settings)` gives the
review after one held on `last` (the business date when left out).

6.2 The next review is in the month after `last`, on the same day of the
month as `last`, or on `reorder.review_day` when that is set. When the month
has no such day, the review is on its last day: after 2027-01-31 comes
2027-02-28, after 2028-01-30 comes 2028-02-29. After a review in December
comes one in January of the next year.

6.3 A `review_day` outside 1 to 31 raises `SettingsError`.

## 1. Rate tables

1.1 A carrier publishes a rate table per service as a JSON object:

| `effective` | first day the table applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` |

| `bands` | list of `{"up_to_kg": n, "cents": c}`, `up_to_kg` rising |
| `over_per_kg_cents` | price of each kilogram above the last band (default 0) |
| `zones` | factor per destination zone, as strings: `{"1": "1.00", "2": "1.18"}` |
| `fuel_pct` | fuel surcharge in percent (default 0) |

3.2 A zone the table does not list raises `RateError`.

received date, then lot id). A transfer moves units lot by lot; the lots keep

site already holds are added to it.

2.2 `lots(sku, site)` lists the lots in stock, oldest first.

4.1 `aging(as_of, site)` lists every lot in stock as `(sku, lot, qty, age)`,

4.2 Rows are sorted oldest first (highest age), then by sku, then by lot id.

5.1 Daily demand is the number of units issued over the `reorder.demand_days`

number of days, rounded half to even to 4 places.

5.2 The reorder point is daily demand times (lead days of the item plus

5.3 `suggestions(ledger, catalog, settings, as_of, site)` gives one suggestion

reorder point plus the demand until the next review (daily demand times the
days from `as_of` to the next review, rounded up), and at least one case.

6.1 Stock is reviewed once a month. `next_review(last, settings)` gives the
review after one held on `last` (the business date when left out).

6.2 The next review is in the month after `last`, on the same day of the
month as `last`, or on `reorder.review_day` when that is set. When the month
has no such day, the review is on its last day: after 2027-01-31 comes

## 1. Rate tables

1.1 A carrier publishes a rate table per service as a JSON object:

| `effective` | first day the table applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `currency` | currency code of every amount |
| `bands` | list of `{"up_to_kg": n, "cents": c}`, `up_to_kg` rising |
| `over_per_kg_cents` | price of each kilogram above the last band (default 0) |

3.4 `to_grams(value, unit)` gives whole grams, rounded half to even.

## 1. Format

1.2 A cell of `None` is empty; `True` and `False` are written `yes` and `no`;

# Bins and putaway

## 1. Bin codes

1.1 A bin code is an aisle letter, a two-digit bay and a one-digit level,
joined by hyphens: `C-07-2` is aisle C, bay 7, level 2. Bays start at `01`
and levels at `1` (the floor). Anything else raises `BinError`.

1.2 `parse_code` gives `(aisle, bay, level)` with aisle A as 0.

## 2. The layout

2.1 A layout is a list of bin records: `code`, `dims_mm` (inner length, width
and height in millimetres), `max_kg` (load limit in whole kilograms) and
`zones` (default `["ambient"]`).

2.2 A layout may list a bin more than once, for example once per zone it
belongs to. Records of one code are one bin: their zones are merged. Records
of one code with different sizes or load limits raise `BinError`.

2.3 An item with a `zone` may only go to bins of that zone. An item without a
zone may go to any bin.

## 3. Choosing a bin

3.1 The walking cost from the origin `putaway.origin` to a bin is

    4 x |aisle difference| + 2 x |bay difference| + 3 x (level - 1)

The origin's own level does not count.

3.2 A pallet of `qty` units fits a bin when its weight is within the load
limit, the item fits the bin in some orientation (sorted item dimensions each
at most the sorted bin dimensions), and `qty` times the item volume is at
most `putaway.max_fill` times the bin volume.

3.3 `choose_bin(item, layout, settings, qty, occupied)` returns the code of the
bin with the lowest walking cost among the bins that are allowed for the item
(2.3), not in `occupied`, and fit the pallet (3.2). When several bins have the
lowest cost, the bin with the smallest code wins, comparing codes as strings:
`A-04-1` before `B-02-1`. When no bin qualifies it raises `NoBinError`.

3.4 The result depends only on the layout's bins, the item, the quantity, the
occupied bins and the settings. The order in which the layout lists its bins
does not matter.

## 4. Putaway

4.1 `putaway(lines, catalog, layout, settings, occupied)` plans a receipt.
`lines` is a list of `(sku, qty)`. A line becomes pallets of `case_qty` units,
the last one holding what is left. Pallets are placed in receipt order, each
with `choose_bin`; a bin that receives a pallet is occupied for the pallets
after it.

4.2 The plan is a list of `(sku, qty, bin)`, one per pallet, in placement
order.

- `tools/ci.py`: `--list` prints the order of a run without running it.

## 2.6.2 (2027-02-16)

- `tools/ci.py`: `-k` keeps the order the tests have in the full run, so a
  subset of a logged run can be repeated in its original order.
- `docs/rates.md` explains when two rate tables are the same table.

## 2.6.1 (2027-01-27)

- Weight conversions multiply first and round once, at the end (`settings.md` 3.2); 2.6.0 rounded the value before converting it.
- `docs/stock.md` gives examples of review dates at the end of a month.

## 2.6.0 (2027-01-18)

- Freight quotes use the volume weight when it is above the actual weight
  (`rates.md` 2.1).
- Rate tables are parsed once and kept in a cache (`rates.md` 4).
- `bins.putaway` places pallets of `case_qty` units.

## 2.5.4 (2026-12-02)

- Exports go through a spool file and replace the target in one step
  (`exports.md` 2.3).
- `reorder.next_review` takes `reorder.review_day`.

## 2.5.0 (2026-10-20)

- Settings sections (`rounding`, `reorder`, `putaway`) can be overridden key
  by key (`settings.md` 2.2).
- `Ledger.aging` and the aging file.

steps.message:
I found six root causes in the logs and fixed all of them. The report is in `/app/flaky-report.json` and the status in `/app/STATUS.json`. All 90 tests pass under UTC, Asia/Tokyo and America/Los_Angeles with `STOCKROOM_NOW=2027-01-31T23:30:00Z`. I didn't run other hash seeds or shuffled orders.

| Class | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `shared-state` | `settings.py:41` | `resolve` copied `DEFAULTS` shallowly, so section overrides changed the defaults for later calls. It now deep-copies. |
| `timezone` | `clock.py:29` | `today()` used the local date. It now uses the UTC date. |
| `clock` | `reorder.py:44` | `next_review` raised `ValueError` when the next month was shorter, for example after the 31st. It now uses the month's last day and rejects a `review_day` of 0. |
| `hash-order` | `bins.py:106` | `choose_bin` broke distance ties by set order. It now breaks them by smallest code. |
| `temp-file` | `export.py:39` | All writers shared one spool file in the system temp directory, opened in append mode. Each writer now gets its own unique spool file in the target's directory and deletes it if the export fails. |
| `cache-key` | `rates.py:86` | The rate-table cache key left out most of the spec. It is now the full spec as sorted JSON, and a spec that isn't plain JSON raises `RateError`. |

For `settings.py` and `bins.py` there are two plausible lines. I filed the shallow copy at line 41 and the `min` call at line 106. The line that actually changes the defaults is 49, and the set is built at line 103.

`test_from_today` appears under both `timezone` and `clock`, because it failed for each cause in different runs.

I also fixed two float problems that no logged failure showed: `billable_kg` now uses integer arithmetic, and `max_fill` is compared as a `Decimal`.

Two kinds of failure got no entry:
- **Fixed in 2.6.1:** the `test_pound_conversion` and `test_to_grams` failures in 2.6.0 runs.
- **Cancelled runs:** the `test_reprice_catalog` errors, which ended in `KeyboardInterrupt` when an operator cancelled runs 1251 and 1283.
